$comment: The engines the interface can choose between. ESCAP requires two that differ in kind, at least one open-weights, declared before 30 September and unchanged after. The API key for a hosted engine is never written here: it is read from LEXDROID_HOSTED_API_KEY in the environment, because a key on disk is a key in a backup.

engines.label: Engine A
engines.weaknesses: Quantised to 4 bits. Reads a long provision in one pass at 16k context; a longer section is split, and a definition that sits outside the split is not seen.
engines.notes: Runs on this machine, or on a GPU rented by the hour. The whole pipeline runs on it alone, which is the Section 3 claim: no proprietary API is called and the weights are open.

engines.label: Engine B
engines.weaknesses: Proprietary and reached over the network, so a run depends on Google's availability, pricing and rate limits, and on the model version continuing to be served; the weights cannot be inspected or run elsewhere. Pinned to a named version rather than a -latest alias, so the declaration does not change underneath the run. Until 26 September 2026 this declaration named Qwen on Groq (qwen/qwen3-32b, then qwen/qwen3.8-27b after Groq retired the first); the free tier's limit of 1,000 output tokens a minute refused every full-size reading, so that engine could not in practice read.
engines.notes: Differs from Engine A in kind on every axis ESCAP names: a commercial hosted model against open weights run locally, a different model and size, and someone else's hardware. One commercial hosted engine and one open-weights engine is the pairing the submission checklist asks for. The Section 3 claim rests on Engine A alone, which runs the whole pipeline with no proprietary API. Needs LEXDROID_HOSTED_API_KEY in the environment; verify with: npm run -w backend engine-check -- --engine engine-b
